subject: TidalCare — increased latency and answer drift after v2.1 upgrade
messages:
From: James Nolan <james@tidalcare.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: TidalCare Support <support@tidalcare.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production impact after v2.1 model upgrade

Hi Camila —

We started seeing a sustained p95 latency increase (~1400ms -> ~2600ms) and a jump in parsing errors for our discharge-summary flow immediately after the v2.1 model rollout last night. A subset of requests are also returning shorter/less-specific answers (examples attached). This is affecting our triage UI and causing manual intervention.

Can Redwood share whether anything changed beyond the model weights (e.g., int8 profile, kernel changes, batching defaults)? We rolled back on our side but still see degraded behavior in the last 30m.

Appreciate quick help — this is customer-impacting today.

—James
Director of Platform — TidalCare

Attachments: sample-requests-errlog.txt
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: James Nolan <james@tidalcare.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after v2.1 model upgrade

Thanks James — sorry for the disruption. We rolled v2.1 at 02:00 UTC and it included two planned changes: (1) model architecture patch (minor head reorder) and (2) adopt a new int8 quantization profile for that variant to reduce token cost. No runtime kernel swaps were scheduled.

We're pulling perf traces and sample payloads now. Mateo (engine) and Priyom (ops) are on it — looping them in. I'll update within 60 minutes with top-level impact and recommended mitigations.

Quick ask for you: can you share the busiest endpoint name and 3 representative request IDs from the last hour? That will speed triage.

—Camila
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: initial findings on TidalCare regression

Team — quick notes from the first 45m of investigation:
- Observed a 1.6–1.9x increase in decode time for the affected variant on A100 pools (p95 decode from 900ms -> 1700ms).
- KV-cache hit rates unchanged. CPU scheduling looks normal.
- The int8 profile applied for v2.1 produces smaller kernels but slightly different attention reorder, which appears to trigger longer attention repositioning on sequences with heavy biomedical tokenization (the discharge-summary flow).
- We also see a correlated drop in token-level confidence on several prompt classes — manifests as shorter, less-specific outputs (James' samples).

Immediate mitigations proposed:
1) Roll back to v2.0 quant profile (fastest near-term).
2) Temporarily pin TidalCare's route to v2.0 model variant (routing policy).
3) Create a targeted qprofile tuning job for biomedical token distributions (medium-term).

I'll spin a constrained benchmark across 50k sample requests from their logs to confirm. Priyom, can you prepare a canary rollback for their dedicated pool?

—Mateo
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: initial findings on TidalCare regression

I kicked off a route pin and scheduled a targeted rollback for the TidalCare Dedicated pool. Plan:
- 11:20 PST: pin route -> v2.0 on 3 nodes (canary).
- 11:35 PST: expand to full pool if canary passes smoke tests (latency and parsing checks).
- 12:15 PST: share customer-facing summary and rollback confirmation.

Also attaching a quick perf snapshot (perf-snapshot-20261121.csv) from the first 30m. Initial canary will include both traffic-weighted and worst-case sequences.

Note: we should coordinate a short executive note for the CRO and the CPO — James pinged for executive attention. Grace, can you prepare a 3-bullet summary for them?

—Priyom
Senior Ops — Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after v2.1 model upgrade

James — quick update and next steps:

What happened: our v2.1 rollout included a new int8 quantization profile that reduced cost but altered attention execution characteristics on heavy biomedical token sequences. That change increased decode latency and reduced answer specificity for some of your discharge-summary prompts.

Immediate actions we took:
- Pinned your route to v2.0 and started a staged rollback at 11:20 PST; canary passed smoke checks at 11:32 PST.
- Expanded rollback to your full Dedicated pool at 11:45 PST.

Observed impact after rollback:
- p95 latency returned to baseline (~1300ms).
- Parsing error rate dropped to pre-upgrade levels.

Next steps (ETA):
- Engineering will run a focused qprofile tuning job for biomedical sequences (48–72 hours).
- We'll provide a patched int8 profile and a validation report before any re-rollout.
- Grace will send a one-page exec note for your leadership and ours.

We apologize for the interruption — we know this hit a critical customer flow. Please let me know if you want a post-mortem call today or tomorrow.

Best,
Camila
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
